summary: Preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated bundled payload
details: The tarball for @servicetitan/mfe-quick-actions@0.5.54 declares a React micro-frontend UI component (main:./dist/index.js with React/mobx dependencies and src/app.tsx), but ships an unrelated preinstall dropper. package.json scripts.preinstall runs `node setup.mjs`, which probes for a system `bun` binary and otherwise downloads `bun-v1.3.13` from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases for the detected platform and architecture, extracts it to a temporary directory, chmods it executable, and uses that freshly-installed runtime to execEile the sibling file math_init.js from the package directory. math_init.js is a 727KB single-line `// @bun @bun-cjs` bundle with obfuscator.io-style identifiers, a large string-constant array, and a rotator function that shifts the array at load — its content cannot be characterized without deobfuscation. The declared React UI purpose has no need for a second JavaScript runtime or an opaque install-time payload; the preinstall path executes attacker-controlled code on the installer's machine on every `npm install`, and the use of a downloaded alternate runtime evades scanners that only trace Node-resolved code. The @servicetitan namespace and UI-library shape are inconsistent with the shipped install-time behavior, matching a compromised-publisher / namespace-hijack pattern.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
